title: Income Annuities Tax Operations: Federal Withholding Rate on Arrears Installments to Beneficiaries
content:
Federal tax on an arrears installment paid on an Ashgrove Income Annuities period-certain contract is withheld at a rate chosen by whose election governs the payee.

1. **The payee's own election.** When the payee has a withholding election of their own on file — a withholding election filed under the payee's own customer profile — federal tax is withheld at the rate on that election (the latest one filed).
2. **Payee other than the owner, no election of their own.** When the payee is a beneficiary or survivor other than the owner and has no withholding election of their own, federal tax is withheld at the payee default rate of **10% (0.10)**, because an election made by the owner does not govern another person's payments.
3. Where neither describes the payee, neither of these rates applies.

| Payee recorded on the contract | Election under the payee's own profile | Rate |
|---|---|---|
| Beneficiary other than the owner | Yes, at 20% | 20% |
| Beneficiary other than the owner | Yes, at 0% | 0% |
| Beneficiary other than the owner | None | 10% |
| The owner | None of the payee's own | Neither rule applies |

*Hypothetical figure.* Taxable part of an arrears installment $900.00, payee a daughter named as beneficiary with no election of her own: federal tax is $900.00 multiplied by 10%, that is $90.00. If she had filed her own election at 15%, the federal tax would be $135.00.
